text:
Linking to GEOS 3.13.0, GDAL 3.8.5, PROJ 9.5.1; sf_use_s2() is TRUE
The aim of this note is to examine the different statistical and cartographical sources of interest for the objectives of the REDEC project.

title: Geomatic database of REDEC project
text:
The map of INSEE
The geometry of voting offices has been made available only very recently by INSEE through an automatic recognition of the location of adresses on listings (INSEE, 2023, Proposition de contour des bureaux de vote). The raw map offers a complete coverage of the territory of the departement :









The geometry of map is relatively simple in rural areas where voting offices correspond to the geometry of a commune or an aggregate of communes. But situation is more complex in urban areas.

title: Geomatic database of REDEC project
text:
Generalisation of the map
We have created a simplified map using Voronoï triangulation applied to the geometric center of the area covered by voting offices. As a consequence, some details are lost but the map become more easy to use for topological and spatial analysis.

title: Geomatic database of REDEC project
text:
Cartogram transformation
As we are interested in election, we realize a third version of the map of voting officies where the area is made proportional to the number of registred people (inscrits). We use the presidential election of 2022 as reference.

title: Distribution of seats by departement for Assemblée Nationale and Senat
text:
This short note aims to examine the distribution of seats in the Sénat and the Assemblée Nationale by département in the Metropolitan area of France (excluding Corsica). We propose to test the following hypothesis :

H1: The correlation between the number of seats and population is more important with past census than the present, due to the lack of recent updates.
H2: The relation between the number of seats and the number of registered population in 2024 is characterised by negative residuals in départements with important population growth in recent years and positive residuals in départements with declining or stable population.
H3: The relation between population and number of seats is much lower in the case of the Sénat.

title: Distribution of seats by departement for Assemblée Nationale and Senat
text:
This short note aims to examine the distribution of seats in the Sénat and the Assemblée Nationale by département in the Metropolitan area of France (excluding Corsica). We propose to test the following hypothesis :

H1: The correlation between the number of seats and population is more important with past census than the present, due to the lack of recent updates.
H2: The relation between the number of seats and the number of registered population in 2024 is characterised by negative residuals in départements with important population growth in recent years and positive residuals in départements with declining or stable population.
H3: The relation between population and number of seats is much lower in the case of the Sénat.

title: Distribution of seats by departement for Assemblée Nationale and Senat
text:
Data
We limit our analysis to the département of métroolitan France (excluding Corse). The variables to be explained are :

NBDEP : number of seats at Assemblée Nationale in 2024
NBSEN : number of seats at Sénat in 2024
I2024 : number of registered citizens in voting office at european election of 2024
P1968..P2023 : Total number of inhabitants according to census

title: Distribution of seats by departement for Assemblée Nationale and Senat
text:
(A) Seats and historical population
We examine the correlation between the number of seats by department in 2024 and the total population in the past and present. The objective is to determine which (implicit) census year was used to allocate the number of seats.

Linear correlation










Comment:  The maximum correlation for the Assemblée Nationale occurs in 2010, which seems logical, as it marks the last modification of territorial divisions. The case of the Sénat is trickier, as the maximum correlation is observed in 1990…



Rank correlation
Do we observe a different conclusion if we use the rank correlation ?










Comment:  The conclusion remains the same when we use the more robust rank-correlation indicator, with a maximum in 2010 for the Assemblée Nationale and 1990 for the Sénat. The gap between the two institutions is higher than in the previous case.

title: Distribution of seats by departement for Assemblée Nationale and Senat
text:
(B) Seats and registered citizens in 2024
We propose a model of allocation of seats \(N_i\) according to number of register \(R_i\) but following a power law with a parameter \(\alpha\) indicating if the allocation has been made in strict proportion \(\alpha=1\), or with advantage to smaller départements (\(\alpha < 1\)) or larger départements (\(\alpha > 1\)) :
\(N_i = k.R_i^\alpha\)

The plot does not reveal particular autocorrelation problems: the power model (red) is very similar to the non-linear LOESS estimate (blue). However, we can notice some heteroscedasticity due to important variations in registered population in departments represented by 2 or 3 seats. title: Distribution of seats by departement for Assemblée Nationale and Senat
text:
(C) Benchmarking Sénat and Assemblée Nationale
Without considering population or the number of registered voters, what are the differences between the Sénat and the Assemblée Nationale in terms of political representation? In other words, can we say that the Sénat better represents some départements than the Assemblée Nationale, and vice versa? To answer this question, we can estimate the number of seats in the Sénat based on the number of seats in the Assemblée Nationale, using the same model of power relations as in the previous section.










Comment : This correlation diagram underlines the problem introduced by transforming population into a discrete number of seats. As we can see, many départements are characterised by similar allocations of seats, with typical situations like 2 seats in both assemblies (12 cases) or 5 seats in the Assemblée Nationale and 3 in the Sénat (16 cases).

Comment : According to the results of the model, the relation is significant (\(r=0.932\) and \(p <0.001\)), but the coefficient of the power relation is clearly lower than 1 (\(\alpha = 0.79\)) with a confidence interval (\(0.62 < \alpha < 0.97\)). We can therefore establish the following rule :

\(NB.SENAT_i = 0.87 \times (NB.DEPUT_i)^{0.79}\)
This result means that the département with the smallest population (characterised by low population density) will be better represented in the Sénat than in the Assemblée Nationale. This is visible if we convert the number of seats to percentages and compute the difference.










Comment : The map reveals a clear relationship between the population density of départements and their representation in the Sénat (low density) and the Assemblée Nationale (high density). The départements with better representation in the Sénat belong to what is generally called the “diagonale du vide”, from the Ardennes to the Pyrénées. The départements with better representation in the Assemblée Nationale are typically those where the most important cities and metropolitan areas are located (Paris, Lille, Marseille, Nantes, Bordeaux, Toulouse, Montpellier, Grenoble, …).

title: Distribution of seats by departement for Assemblée Nationale and Senat
text:
Discussion
The fact that the Senate presents itself as a chamber representing territories rather than citizens is not in itself shocking. Many countries have, in fact, structured their second chamber not on a basis proportional to population but rather to the number of autonomous political entities. For example, each department could send two representatives to the Senate. One could even imagine each department having representation in the Senate proportional to its area, if the word ‘territory’ is taken in its geometric sense. The Gironde, with an area of 9,976 km², would then have almost 100 times as many senators as the department of Paris, with its 105 km². But one might perhaps hesitate to apply this rule to French Guiana and its 83,856 km²…
The real problem with the current situation is that the Senate nevertheless claims to provide representation proportional to the number of citizens, but does so in a completely biased manner, using a system that penalises the most populous departments (see the power-law parameter \(\alpha = 0.73\)) and based on population figures that appear to date back to 1980. This is therefore a false form of proportionality and a manifestly unfair rule, since departments with the same number of representatives in the Senate may have populations varying by a ratio of 1 to 4.
The observed link between population density and over-representation in the Senate, compared with the National Assembly, is largely an artefact. It results from an imperfect proportionality law combined with an outdated census reference framework that favours territories whose populations have grown the least. If one were genuinely to ensure objective representation for the least densely populated territories, a new measure would need to be devised, combining, for example, the share of the population and the share of the departments’ total area according to a precise rule of the following type:
\(Weight_i = (\frac{Area_i}{Total_area})^\mu \times (\frac{Pop_i}{Total_pop})^{1-\mu}\)
But are departments really the best level at which to make decisions?

Suppose now that we use as initial building blocks the division in 804 voting offices, withour considering the limits of communes as a constraint. In the case of Val-de-Marne, the size of voting office is very regular because each commune has a sufficient population to have several voting office.And we can suppose that their maximum size is defined by the law.


`stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value `binwidth`.

It is therefoer a demographic space whee the distance between two point is not a number of kilometers but a number of people. What is called by the sociologist Samuel Stouffer (1942) an amount of intervening opportunities.









The coordinates in this demographic space to benefit from some interesting properties and make possible to use existing algorithm of classification. title: K-means clustering in demographic space
section: 4. K-means in demographic space with equal size constraint
text:
4. K-means in demographic space with equal size constraint
Some authors has developped methods that take into account a constraint of equal size of cluster. As an example we have use the function balanced_cluster() of the package anticluster which make possible to obtain cluster with exacly the same number of individuals. Unfortunately the authors of the package has decided that “exactly means exactly” … which means that we are obliged to “cheat” our data if the number of units can not be divided by the number of expected cluster … In our example, we have 804 units to be divided in 11 circonscription and the program does not work as it can not be divided by 11 without decimal. But if we aggregate only two offices with their neighbors, we arrive at 803 units which can be divided by 11 \(803/11 ==73\)
The algorithm will produce circonscriptions with the same number of voting office. And as the voting office has generally equivalent size, the result will be approximatively equivalent when we aggregate.

title: K-means clustering in demographic space
text:
Discussion
This analysis confirms that the legal obligation to build circonscription has aggregates of communes limits the possibility to reach optimal solutions and create a legal confusion between two elections. The cantons are instrument of local elections (département) when circonscription are instrument of national elections. Using the voting office as building blocks would be more logical if we admit that a member of the parliament is not defending a local area but elabrating national policy …

text: This github directory is used for cartographic experiments in relation with the submission of the REDEC project to the AAPG 2026 of the ANR. We will more precisely focus onthe analysis of four cases studies related to the département of Isère, Maine-et-Loire, Somme and Val-de-Marne.

title: REDEC
text:
Selection of cases studies
Four département has been carefully chosen as places of experiment of the different methods and concepts developed in previous work packages. These four case studies will be used ex-ante in order to test methods and concepts that will be further applied to the whole territory of France. They will also be used ex-post as proof of concept for researcher and decision maker. And finally they will be used as test for the research of the best way to disseminate the results toward stakeholders and citizens. To achieve this objectives, the four cases studies has been chosen in order to represent both geographical complexity and political diversity of situations :
– Val-de-Marne (94) is a metropolitan département located in the suburb of Paris with a very high population density concentrated in very few communes which implies necessarily to break some of them in order to have equal population size in cantons. The political opinion is characterized by equivalent proportion of votes for left and center-right but very few votes for far-right.
– Isère (38) offers the case of a département which combines very strong geographical and political differences. The density of population is very high in the metropolitan agglomeration of Grenoble and the related valleys but very low in mountains area. The political diversity is complete with far-right in the north, far-left in the suburb of Grenoble and center-left or center right elsewhere.
– Somme (80) is a good example of rural and industrial area that has been exposed to economic crisis and has recently offers a majority of vote to far-right, with the exception of the capital city of Amiens. Furthermore, the strange shape of some of its districts raises questions. It is also a remarkable case of gerrymandering with three strange circonscriptions having the form of an octopus (n°4) and a salamander (n°1) surrounding a frog (n°2) …
– Maine-et-Loire (49) located in the Western part of France is the opposite example of Somme in political terms as it remains a typical area or resistance of center-right or center-left.It is also characterized by an interesting administrative evolution with a strong reduction of the number of communes by merging (Bideau 2024). We arrive at a moment where some cluster of rural communes are larger than cantons.

The aim of this note is to examine the different statistical and cartographical sources of interest for the objectives of the REDEC project.

title: Geomatic database of REDEC project
text:
The map of INSEE
The geometry of voting offices has been made available only very recently by INSEE through an automatic recognition of the location of adresses on listings (INSEE, 2023, Proposition de contour des bureaux de vote). The raw map offers a complete coverage of the territory of the departement :









The geometry of map is relatively simple in rural areas where voting offices correspond to the geometry of a commune or an aggregate of communes. But situation is more complex in urban areas.

title: Geomatic database of REDEC project
text:
Generalisation of the map
We have created a simplified map using Voronoï triangulation applied to the geometric center of the area covered by voting offices. As a consequence, some details are lost but the map become more easy to use for topological and spatial analysis.

title: Geomatic database of REDEC project
text:
Cartogram transformation
As we are interested in election, we realize a third version of the map of voting officies where the area is made proportional to the number of registred people (inscrits). We use the presidential election of 2022 as reference.

Filosofi 2021
The INSEE grid of population Filosofi at the resolution of 200m x 200m has been published in 2021 with a set of 30 indicators describing the population by age and sex and some economic and social indicator derived from census like the median income of the houshold, the share of social housing, etc. This resolution of 200m is generally sufficient to charactrize the situation of voting office, even if some approximation is requested in central urban area. title: Visualisation tool
text:
We propose to visualize the delineation of circonscription with two complementary maps.


We use here the classical map in geometric space with eucldean distance. We can therefore viusalize large surfaces corresponding to low density area and small surfaces corresponding to high density area.












We use here a cartogramme transformation of voting office in order to produce a demographic space where the area is proportional to the number of people officially allowed to vote. The distance between two points is the number of inhabitant between origin and destination (the Stouffer distance).
